analysis:
Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi stated that India had achieved 50% of installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources, five years ahead of the 2030 target.

PIB data for 30 June 2025 showed non-fossil capacity (renewables, large hydro and nuclear) at 242.78 GW of 484.82 GW, or 50.08%. CEA data for 30 June 2026 showed non-fossil capacity at 297.37 GW, or 54.18% of 548.86 GW installed.

The 50% milestone refers to installed capacity; the share of renewable sources in actual electricity generation is lower, and press analysis noted fossil fuels still supplied the majority of generation. The installed-capacity milestone as stated is supported by CEA and PIB data, so the claim is recorded as true.
notes: Joshi's quotation is from the PIB release, which reproduces his statement; because it is an official release rather than a speech transcript it is not marked verbatim. The PIB release is dated 14 July 2025 and the ETEnergyworld report of a related speech is dated 20 July 2025.
